terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase; Terence’s rēctē putās is the attested one.

evidence: Plaut. Capt. 1.2.73; Ter. Eun. 2.2.57, 3.1.37 (Lewis & Short s.v. facētus)
terms.comment: Praise for a witty remark rather than a true one: facētē, wittily.

phrases.english: “He didn’t bring it! The Minotaur stays at Conimbriga!” “You’re right.”
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 107, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026.
